items.title: PDEformer-2: a versatile foundation model for two-dimensional partial differential equations
items.summary: Abstract Partial differential equations (PDEs) are fundamental to modeling physical systems. Traditional PDE solvers are often computationally expensive. Neural operators require independent training for different PDEs, and tend to be data-greedy when adapted to new scenarios. To this end, we introduce PDEformer-2, a versatile foundation model for solving diverse two-dimensional PDEs. The model receives the PDE form as input through a flexible computational graph representation and outputs solutions that can be queried at any spatio-temporal point. Pretrained on a 40 TB dataset spanning varied equation types, domains, boundary conditions, variable counts, and time dependence, PDEformer-2 enables instant zero-shot predictions for familiar PDEs and adapts faster to unseen ones than specialized baselines, achieving lower errors with limited samples. It also facilitates efficient inverse problem solving, successfully recovering unknown PDE parameters, including scalar coefficients and fields, in experiments.

items.title: Air-gap engineering enabled ultrafast 9-bit ferroelectric semi-gate transistor array for high-efficiency image denoising
items.summary: Abstract The insufficient lateral electric field gradient limits the programming/erasing speed of conventional semi-floating gate transistors, while charge leakage leads to poor data retention and compromised operating characteristics. Here we design a ferroelectric semi-gate (FSG) transistor featuring a triangular air gap adjacent to the drain region. The device exhibits an as-programmed on–off ratio exceeding 10 7 , remaining above 10 5 after 11 weeks, and a memory window of approximately 6 V. The localized lateral electric field accelerates program and erase operations to 60 ns and 75 ns, respectively. The spontaneous polarization field of the ferroelectric HfZrO layer strengthens charge retention in the HfO 2 charge-trapping layer, enabling robust nonvolatile memory performance with a retention time exceeding 10 6 s. This synergistic integration of air-gap engineering and ferroelectric polarization yields an optimal trade-off between speed, retention and multilevel operation. By exploiting its superior multilevel capability with 9-bit distinguishable current states, we realize Ising-model-based image denoising using a 32 × 32 transistor array. These FSG transistors show promising potential for high-speed, low-power random-access memory applications.

Global hotspots and trends of ecological water scarcity in river basins
items.summary: Abstract Healthy freshwater ecosystems are crucial for sustainable development, yet they face growing threats from unsustainable water use. However, current water scarcity metrics focus almost exclusively on human demand, overlooking whether sufficient water remains to sustain ecosystems. We address this gap by presenting the first evaluation of ecological water scarcity (EWS) across 1,182 river basins, introducing a novel indicator that recognizes ecosystems as legitimate water users to those of humans. Our findings reveal that in the 2000s, 412 basins (35% globally; 17% annual, 18% seasonal) experienced EWS, with affected areas expanding by 10 million km² since the 1950s. Human intervention intensified EWS in 13% of basins and caused 53% of seasonal and 60% of annual EWS cases. By the 2050s, affected basins range from 392 under RCP2.6–SSP1 to 416 under RCP8.5–SSP5, with persistent hotspots in regions of intensive water use. These findings show that climate mitigation can reduce future EWS risk, but environmental flow protection, water-use efficiency, water recycling, ecologically informed infrastructure operation and ecosystem restoration are also needed to safeguard freshwater ecosystems.

items.title: Rate-limited nonradiative recombination at a single point defect revealed by time-resolved cathodoluminescence
authors: Thomas F. K. Weatherley, Gunnar Kusch, Jean-François Carlin, Raphaël Butté, Rachel A. Oliver, and Nicolas Grandjean
items.summary: K. Weatherley, Gunnar Kusch, Jean-François Carlin, Raphaël Butté, Rachel A. Oliver, and Nicolas Grandjean Nonradiative point defects in semiconductors are often a major hurdle for efficiency and reliability in optoelectronics, yet directly probing these defects remains difficult. This study uses time-resolved cathodoluminescence mapping plus a diffusion-recombination model to isolate and quantify carrier dynamics at a single point defect in an (In,Ga)N/GaN quantum well. Recombination at the defect is rate-limited by a 16-ps delay, setting a hard bottleneck on defect activity. This insight predicts that defect-related nonradiative recombination saturates at carrier densities routinely reached in LEDs, revealing a fundamental limit not captured by traditional macroscale recombination models.

This work uses constrained variational optimization with epitaxial-growth-motivated constraints to design feasible germanium concentration profiles in Si/Si-Ge quantum wells, to enhance deterministic valley splitting while suppressing variability induced by alloy disorder. The principal result is a “modulated wiggle well”, which provides a large, robust, and electrically tunable valley splitting. The approach provides a systematic route for designing reproducible and epitaxially feasible silicon-qubit devices.

items.title: Colloquium: Laboratory exploration of planetary interiors
authors: G. W. Collins, S. Seager, J. Eggert, X. Gong, M. Huff, J. R. Rygg, T.-A. Suer, and R. Jeanloz
items.summary: W. Collins, S. Seager, J. Eggert, X. Gong, M. Huff, J. R. Rygg, T.-A. Suer, and R. Jeanloz Astronomers observe thousands of planets beyond our Solar System, many with extreme interior conditions. Deep inside these worlds, gravity produces pressures millions to billions of times stronger than Earth’s atmosphere. At these pressures, matter behaves in surprising ways: hydrogen can become metallic, water and ammonia may form exotic superionic states, and hydrocarbons can turn into diamond. This Colloquium describes how studying these unusual materials helps scientists explain how planets form, evolve, and generate magnetic fields and magma oceans. Using powerful lasers and pulsed-power facilities, researchers recreate such pressures in laboratories, revealing new physics and improving understanding of the hidden interiors of distant planets.
